lesson.title: Chặng 1: C# cơ bản và ứng dụng console

learning_objectives.statement: Build and explain a small console expense flow from a blank file using validated input, a loop, a method, and a collection.
Record actual behavior for invalid input, empty state, exit handling, and one debugger or failure-path observation.

activity.title: Stage 01 console expense app evidence
activity.instructions:
This bounded activity covers the console expense flow from DotNet-React-Roadmap/1.md.
It is a guided self-study evidence task, not the complete Stage 01 gate or a
substitute for the independent learner checks in the roadmap.

Prerequisites: use the .NET 10 LTS SDK on Windows, a Windows editor such as Visual Studio Code with the
C# Dev Kit or Visual Studio, and a terminal with basic dotnet CLI familiarity.
In a learner-owned scratch folder, create a console project with dotnet new
console, and keep this work separate from any course source files.

Build the first expense-console slice from an empty Program.cs: accept a
category and non-negative amount, repeat an input/menu loop, add valid entries,
list entries, show a running total, and stop on the documented exit choice.
Split at least one input or calculation responsibility into a method. Include
a List<T> or equivalent collection and deliberately observe its empty-state
behavior. Exercise valid input, empty input, text where a number is expected,
a negative amount, an exit choice, and an empty list before the first entry.

Submit an evidence note containing the exact commands used, learner-chosen
inputs, actual observed outputs, the method/loop boundary you can explain,
and one debugger observation or a recorded step-through of a failure path.
Do not invent output, timing, debugger state, or results. If the SDK, editor,
or terminal is unavailable, leave the activity incomplete and record the
blocker; an environment blocker is not successful completion.

Keep the full-stage checks separate from this guided evidence: independently
rewrite the expense app from a blank file, reach at least five entries, handle
input text/empty/negative/list-empty cases, identify one logic error with a
breakpoint, and assess whether adding an expense date preserves the menu.
Those checks are not claimed by this activity unless independently evidenced.
activity.expected_output: A learner evidence note with real console inputs, outputs, loop/method reasoning, and a recorded boundary observation

rubric.evidence: The note shows actual category and amount inputs, valid and invalid paths, a repeatable menu or loop, and observed list/total behavior without fabricated output.
The note records empty input, text where a number is expected, a negative amount, exit handling, and the empty-list path, with the learner explaining the chosen validation and List behavior.
The note explains one method boundary and records a real debugger observation or step-through of a chosen failure path; unavailable tooling remains incomplete.
